text:
maya: quick async — i'm finalizing the docs + a tiny contract change for /v1/embeddings and want alignment on a few edge behaviors before i open the PR. TL;DR: mixed input types, truncation strategy, batch size semantics, and output shape for empty items.

ajay: thanks — enumerating the questions would help, thx.

maya: sure — 1) if callers send a mix of strings and bytes (utf-8), do we coerce bytes -> string or return 400? 2) when an item exceeds the per-item token limit, do we: truncate, split into multiple embeddings, or reject? 3) batch_size param: is it max items per request or max items per internal batch (i.e., we may shard request into N internal batches if > batch_size)? 4) empty string vs null vs missing field: what vector do we return? zeros, error, or omit? 5) response ordering guarantee for async parallelization?

leo: quick answers based on runtime behavior: 1) we currently accept bytes and coerce to utf-8 string, replacing invalid sequences with U+FFFD (this is what the ingest path does). if it's non-utf8 binary we end up with replacement chars.

sarah: 2) per-item exceed — we used to truncate at token boundary, but there's an ongoing split-vs-truncate debate. current default is TRUNCATE with a telemetry flag. split into multiple embeddings causes ordering & id mapping complexity for customers.

maya: ok noted. i want the documented default to match runtime. so default=truncate, and we add a flag split_long_inputs=true to opt into split+concatenate semantics?

ajay: that seems reasonable. follow-ups: what about per-request batch_size vs internal sharding?

leo: batch_size in the API is a hint for client-side chunking. server-side we have an internal max_batch_capacity (by dimensions & memory). if request.items > internal_capacity we shard transparently and then reassemble in-order before responding. so API preserves ordering. however the config param name currently is "batch_size_hint" in the client SDK.

maya: let's standardize to "batch_size" in the public API and keep it as a hint. we'll document that server may shard and that ordering is preserved. can we also document potential increased latency if server shards?

ops-bot: deploy status: embeddings-runtime v3.14 rolled canary -> 3% earlier today, no errors so far.

sarah: 4) empty input behavior — currently: empty string -> deterministic zero-vector; null -> 400; omitted field -> 400. we should consider returning zero-vector for null too for UX. but watch for downstream semantics where zero-vector is a valid semantic embedding (rare but possible).

leo: we can add an explicit sentinel input type: {"text": "", "treat_empty_as": "zero"} but that complicates payload. i'd prefer we: empty string => zero-vector (keep), null => 400 with clear error message suggesting to send "" if they want zero-vector behavior.

maya: agree with leo. i'll document: empty string -> zeros; null or missing -> 400 with error code EMBED_MISSING_FIELD.

ajay: 5) ordering — confirm: we preserve order of items in response regardless of internal sharding. also, do we include item-level ids in the response so clients can reconcile?

leo: yes we return an array of embeddings in the same order as input array. we also include optional ids if caller provides an "id" field per item; otherwise we return index-based implicit ids. current response shape example:

[{
  "id": "user-provided-id-123",
  "embedding": [0.000123, -0.00234, ...],
  "model": "redwood-embed-2-small"
}]

maya: please note: vectors are float32 and we quantize for some backends — response numeric precision should be documented. also need to document length: fixed dim per model (e.g., 1536 for embed-2-small).

sarah: code review ping @leo @ajay — i added the error code EMBED_MISSING_FIELD and examples to the docs branch. can you look at the error wording? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/492

ajay: will review today. small ask: include an explicit example of a mixed input request with bytes + strings + ids. example request in docs should reflect coercion semantics.

maya: adding an example here for the thread — please sanity-check: 

POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-2-small",
  "items": [
    {"id": "a", "text": "hello world"},
    {"id": "b", "text": "caf\\u00e9"},
    {"id": "c", "data": "SGVsbG8sIHdpdGggYnl0ZXMgYmFzZTY0"} // base64 bytes payload accepted -> coerced to utf-8
  ],
  "batch_size": 64
}

leo: note: we actually don't accept base64 in "data" by default; we'd only accept raw bytes over the SDK/transport. if docs show base64 it should be in the SDK example, not the raw HTTP. change to a comment: "SDK will send bytes via binary field".

sarah: good catch. i'll update examples.

maya: next: truncation granularity — do we truncate by token or by codepoint/utf8 bytes? current runtime truncates on tokenization boundary (we use the tokenizer to compute token length). we'll document "truncates at token boundary to the model's context window."

ajay: any telemetry flags or heuristics to prefer split if semantic chunking detected? we had a flag to split on sentence boundaries once a month for experiments. please document that as experimental and behind a feature flag.

leo: added: telemetry "embed.split_long_inputs" boolean, default=false. experimental behavior: if true and input > limit, we split on sentence boundaries, call embeddings for each chunk, and average the chunk vectors. this is opt-in and will be available in SDK 1.8.

maya: great. last logistic: PR for docs will include a small compatibility note: older clients that relied on null->zero vector will see 400; we should send a migration email and add a compatibility header: "X-Embed-Compat: null-zero-v1" available for 30 days. ops, ok?

ops-bot: noted. compatibility header draft created in infra: https://internal.redwood/compat/embeds-null-zero-v1. rolling 30-day warning window will be emitted as telemetry alert for 404 impacted customers.

ajay: +1. can we add an integration test that sends a huge item and asserts truncation and order preserved?

leo: already on my board — adding an end-to-end test in runtime/integration/test_embed_truncation.py. i'll add the test id to the PR.

maya: awesome. i'll open the docs PR after adjusting the SDK example + adding the compatibility note. tagging for final review: @leo @ajay @sarah. if no objections by EOD i'll merge and schedule the PR to go live with the next docs deploy. :thumbsup:

dev-bot: reminder queued: docs dep deploy scheduled 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z.

maya: thanks all. leaving this thread open for follow-ups.

ajay: thanks — quick follow: should we mention numeric dtype (float32) vs compressed (int8) in the response examples so customers don't assume binary layout?

leo: yes, doc note: "embeddings are returned as JSON array of floats (float32 precision). Some backends store/transfer compressed representations internally; API always returns floats."

sarah: added that sentence in the PR.

maya: perfect. closing the loop here. if anyone finds a mismatch in runtime vs docs, ping me and i'll revert the merge.

leo: noted.

maya: end.
